title: Linear Functions, Part 1: The Idea and an Easy Problem

beats.say: A linear function changes by the same amount every time its input goes up by one. That steady change is what makes its graph a straight line.

card.text: Same change for every step in x

beats.say: On the SAT, you'll evaluate functions written in function notation, find a slope from two points or a table, and read intercepts from an equation.
You'll also interpret what the numbers mean in a real situation, such as a cost model where one number is a starting fee and another is a price per item.
In the function f of x equals m x plus b, the number m is the slope, which is the rate of change. The number b is f of zero, which is the y-intercept.
beats.item: f(x) = mx + b: slope m, intercept b

beats.say: The notation f of four means put four in for x. That's different from the question, for what x is f of x equal to four, which asks you to set the expression equal to four and solve.
Slope is the change in output divided by the change in input. Any two points on the same line give the same slope.
beats.item: Slope = change in output over input

beats.say: If f of x plus one equals f of x plus three, the slope is three. If f of x plus five equals f of x plus ten, the slope is ten divided by five, which is two.
beats.item: Read the slope from a pattern

beats.say: In a model, the slope is the rate, such as dollars per mile, and the intercept is the starting value when the input is zero.
beats.item: Model: slope is rate, intercept is start

beats.say: Lines are often written in one of two forms. In the first, f of x equals m x plus b, you can read the slope m and the y-intercept zero comma b directly.
In the second form, called point-slope form, you read the slope m and a point the line passes through. This form is handy when a question gives you a point and a slope.
To find the slope from two points, divide the change in y by the change in x. This is often remembered as rise over run.
The order matters only in one way. If y two is on top, then x two must be on the bottom, in the same order, so that the signs stay consistent.

card.text: Keep the same order top and bottom

beats.say: Easy example. The function f is defined by f of x equals seven minus two x. Find f of negative three, and find the value of x for which f of x equals negative five.

card.sub: Find f(−3), and x when f(x) = −5

beats.say: The notation f of negative three means replace x with negative three. We write that substitution first, keeping the parentheses around the negative number.
Now multiply. Negative two times negative three is positive six, because a negative times a negative is positive. So the expression becomes seven plus six.
Seven plus six is thirteen. So f of negative three equals thirteen. Notice that the input was negative three, and the output is thirteen.
This time the output is given, and we need the input. So we set the expression equal to negative five and solve, just like a linear equation.
Subtract seven from both sides, so the plain number leaves the left side. Negative five minus seven is negative twelve.
Divide both sides by negative two. Negative twelve divided by negative two is six. So x equals six.
Check part B by putting six back into the function. Seven minus two times six is seven minus twelve, which is negative five. That matches, so x equals six is correct.
To recap. In f of x equals m x plus b, the slope is m and the y-intercept is b.
Evaluating f of a number means substituting it in. Solving f of x equals a number means setting the expression equal to it.
Slope is rise over run, with the same order on top and bottom. In the next video, we work through a medium problem and a hard problem.
